subject: brrrr math when refi fails
preheader: the moment a brrrr stops being a brrrr.
headline: BRRRR only works when the refinance pulls you out. Most don't.
body: BRRRR is Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat. The whole strategy depends on step four — refinancing at 70-75% LTV of the after-repair value and pulling most of your cash back out.

The math: you need ARV × 0.75 to be greater than (or at least equal to) your all-in cost. All-in = purchase + rehab + closing + holding. If that's not true, the refinance leaves cash stuck in the deal, and it stops being a BRRRR — it's just a leveraged rental.

Example: buy at $200,000, rehab $40,000, $10,000 in closing and holding. All-in is $250,000. ARV needs to be $250,000 / 0.75 = $333,333 minimum just to break even on the refi. If your appraiser comes in at $310,000, you get $232,500 back at 75% LTV. You've left $17,500 stuck in the deal.
Most BRRRRs that 'fail' don't fail at the rent step. They fail because the ARV came in under expectations or the rehab ran 20% over. Model both before you buy.

TrueCap Pro includes a BRRRR analyzer that runs this exact math, with sensitivity on both ARV and rehab. If you do BRRRRs, the $19/mo pays for itself the first time a refi appraisal comes in light and you knew about it before you bought.
